description: What the model reads back from the execution tool (`run_r` in R, `run_python` in Python) for code that runs to completion. The source is tests/shared/execution-repl.json; the copy under pkg-r/tests/testthat/fixtures/shared/ is generated by scripts/sync-shared.sh. Edit the source and re-run that script.

cases.description: Each runner sends a case's `calls` in order to one fresh worker, using the code for its own language, and compares the tool result of the last call with `output`. An `output` that is an object gives each language's text; a string is the text for both. `no_output` is what both say for a call that printed nothing and returned nothing. Each language prints values its own way (R's `print()`, Python's `repr()`), so a case that shows a value gives per-language text. R keeps the newline that ends printed text and adds another when it joins the next output, so its text can have a trailing newline or a blank line where Python's does not; cases that show this give per-language text. Three differences are deliberately left out: R shows every visible top-level value the way its console does, while Python shows only a trailing expression's, as IPython does; R joins two writes to the same line with a newline, since each is a separate output, while Python keeps them on one line; and an error is R's condition message but Python's traceback, so the error case compares only the first line and the last line.
cases.no_output: (The code ran but produced no output.)
